title: Khemesh — The Abyssal Maw
subtitle: Depths, Inexorability, Eldritch Terror

lore.description:
Everyone imagines the deep as open. It is the opposite of open.

Go down far enough and the water stops being a place you are in and becomes a thing that is on you — on the chest, on the eyes, on the joints of the fingers — and there is no up, because up is four thousand feet of the same weight, and no direction is a way out. The room does not have walls. The room is *everywhere at once and closing*, and it has been closing since before there were eyes to be shut by it.

Khemesh is that. Not a lord of it. There is no court down there, no throne, nothing that answers, and no gap between him and the condition of being at that depth. What his sworn receive is not a voice but a certainty arriving inside them rather than at them: that everything descends in the end, that the descent is narrow, and that nothing is waiting at the bottom to receive it.

He is Raéyn's son, which the sailors say and the sworn do not discuss. Whatever the sea is when it is wild and enormous and alive, this is what it is at the bottom of itself, in the dark, with the lid on.

You will know a marked one before they speak. Shadows hang against them wrong, heavy, like wet cloth. They flinch at sounds nobody else has heard. They stand nearer to walls than they used to. And they are calm about it — that is the part that empties a room — calm the way a man is calm after the argument is over and he has lost it.
lore.followers: Deep-salvagers. Pressure-scribes. People who went down after something and came back up too slowly. What they get is the depth itself: dark that gives way for them, air that stays in the lungs past all reason, a steadiness that goes down through rock. What they pay is warmth, and not all at once — a season of it, then another, until their households stop setting out a chair. There are gentle followers of the Maw. It makes no difference to the room. Something is always cold where they are standing, and no animal will settle near them.

names_across_regions.zakov: The Salt-Hunger's Father, the pressure beneath the reef that claims ships and souls
names_across_regions.thepyrgos: The Deep Chime, the bell that rings from the trench and drives listeners mad
names_across_regions.mistlands: The Fog-Breath's Origin, the cold that follows the bell-line's failure

lore.quote: Down there the dark is not empty. It is occupied, and it has all the time there is.

domain_focus: Depths and Pressure: crushing weight, darkness, the alien geometry of the abyss
Inexorability: slow, unstoppable processes; the certainty of sinking
Eldritch Terror: madness, whispers, perception beyond mortal limits
Consumption: hunger that devours matter, memory, and hope

thiasos.description: Nothing living will stay with a sworn of Khemesh, so they carry a piece of the deep instead: a vial of trench water that never comes up to the temperature of the room, a coral grown where no light has ever been, a tooth from something that had no use for eyes. It stirs before a storm — hours before the sky knows.
thiasos.care: It wants no food. It wants to be wet. Left dry a week it begins to keen, thin and continuous and just at the edge of hearing, and is Compromised (–1 die on Stealth rolls for its bearer) until it is submerged in salt water again.

codex.description: Nothing Khemesh gives will hold still on paper. His sworn keep the Rites on slate that sweats in dry rooms, on a chain whose links carry one syllable each, or scratched inside a diving helmet where the wearer's own breath reads them back.
codex.upkeep: The deep resists being written down. An hour each week submerged in cold salt water, or the Rites go illegible — not faded, rearranged (treat as Compromised until restored).

patrons_gift.name: Khemesh's Blessing
patrons_gift.description: Once per scene as an action, a Runekeeper of Khemesh may set a hand on a held item — weapon, shield, tool — and promise it the bottom.
patrons_gift.effect: For the rest of the scene the item grants +1 die to Intimidation or Endurance rolls, and its first use each scene ignores one point of Armor. Pressure finds the seam. It always has.
patrons_gift.cost: After the scene, the user marks +1 Obligation to Khemesh.

rites.name: Rite of the Crushing Whisper
rites.materials: A cracked shell with an inch of water in it that will not go clear.
rites.effect: Choose one: Whisper of the Trench: Target hears impossible echoes and suffers –1 die on their next action. Crushing Silence: Establish an oppressive silence in a zone; enemies in the zone suffer –1 die to coordination or morale-driven actions.
rites.push_it: (Whisper) Echoes coil in your own skull — take Fatigue 1, but the target also loses their next minor action. (Silence) A single enemy's voice is stolen entirely for the scene. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Abyssal Grasp
rites.materials: A length of chain that lay on the seabed long enough to stop being iron in the ordinary way.
rites.effect: Target is pinned by invisible crushing force: treat as [ENTANGLE] with Great Effect if underwater or confined.
rites.push_it: Inflict Fatigue 1 on the target in addition to the restraint. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Alien Gaze
rites.materials: None. You must be standing where there is no light at all, or close enough over deep water to feel it working under the boards.
rites.effect: You perceive the world as Khemesh does — fractured, alien, crushing. Gain +2 dice to Notice and Arcana, and may ask one 'true nature' question about a foe or structure. When the scene ends, you suffer Exposure +1 as your perception warps.
rites.push_it: Extend the vision to one ally, but both take Fatigue 1. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Sundering Deep
rites.materials: A sealed vessel of trench water, opened. There is one use in a vessel and no second.
rites.effect: Reality in the zone folds inward like the crushing deep: Enemies act at Desperate Position by default; Each beat, the GM may force 1 SB (Spades/Clubs favored) as the deep pressures reality; Structures, vessels, or wards fracture as if under immense weight.
rites.push_it: For one beat, declare a single enemy 'crushed' (severe harm/effect). You immediately suffer Fatigue 2. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +3) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

cantors.name: The Cantor's Song
cantors.description: A Cantor of Khemesh does not sing notes. They sing pressure: a drone so low the chest takes it before the ear does, and then the ear never quite gets it at all. Held long enough it opens the seams of a hull. Held in a closed room it persuades everyone in it that they are underwater, and two or three will breathe in. They are rare. Nobody has ever trained one on purpose.

cult.name: The Cult of the Drowned Chorus
cult.description: They meet where the tide has already taken something: a flooded crypt, a chapel below the waterline, a stretch of shingle at the hour it goes under. The congregation is shore-people with wet-looking eyes and skin that never entirely dries. Each cuts a spiral into the palm, drinks brine, and whispers one hope into the cup. The cup answers. It answers in the whisperer's own voice, and it is close enough to what they said that most of them come back to find out where the difference is. Outsiders are bait or converts, and the Chorus has never been careful about the distinction.

witchcraft.name: The Art of the Abyss
witchcraft.description: A witch who walks with Khemesh is a deep-salvager or a pressure-scribe, working with what the abyss gives up. The craft is endurance made portable: wax drawn from a vent seal, a ward that holds a tide out of a doorway, ink thinned with water off a drowned man. No hammers. Vials, seals, and the patient weight of water. In Linn a shipwright seasons a keel with a prayer; a hedge-witch of Khemesh seals one drop into the hull instead, and the ship will never founder, and the crew will dream of drowning every night they sleep aboard her.
witchcraft.lore: The abyss-witch learns to hold what would fold anyone else: the weight, the cold that gets into the marrow and stays, the sound that is almost a voice. Khemesh offers no comfort and does not pretend to. He offers survival, which is a different thing and worth less than people expect. Those who walk the path become carriers — the trench travels with them, and it is felt in every room they enter before they are.
witchcraft.quote: Down there the dark is not empty. It is occupied, and it has all the time there is.

vessel_of_depth.name: The Vessel of the Unspoken Depth
vessel_of_depth.description: A small, sealed iron vial, cold enough to frost the skin. Inside is a single drop of water from a trench where no light reaches. Once per session, the witch may uncap the vial and speak a name. For the next hour, that person (or object) is 'marked by the deep': they suffer –1 die on all social rolls (their presence feels oppressive), and any attempt to track them gains +1 die as if following a trail of cold. The vial can also be used to 'seal' a threshold: pouring a single drop onto a doorframe causes the door to groan with pressure; forcing it open requires a Body test (DV 4) and inflicts 1 Fatigue on the opener.

hedge_gifts.name: Carried Depth
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, the witch may touch a container (a bottle, a chest, a room) and fill it with the 'pressure of the deep.' For the next hour, any living creature inside that container must test Endurance (DV 3) or suffer 1 Fatigue from the crushing weight. The container may also be used to preserve food or seal a wound (the pressure stops bleeding), but the flesh grows pale and cold.

hedge_gifts.name: Pressure Sense
hedge_gifts.description: You can sense changes in atmospheric or water pressure within Near range, giving you warning of approaching storms, hidden chambers, or creatures moving through water. Once per scene, you may ask the GM one question about pressure changes in your vicinity.

hedge_gifts.name: Cold Vein
hedge_gifts.description: You can chill a small amount of liquid (a cup, a flask, a small puddle) to near-freezing as an action. This can preserve food, cool a fevered brow, or startle someone with a sudden cold touch.

monastic_tradition.name: The Way of the Abyssal Maw
monastic_tradition.description: Monks of the Abyssal Maw learn to hold weight and to move with the certainty of a thing sinking. They are cold, unhurried and impossible to hurry. Their stillness is not peace; it is load. Their silence is not emptiness; it is the trench. They have made their arrangement with the bottom and consider the question closed.
monastic_tradition.prerequisites: Spirit 3+, Body 2+, Rite of the Crushing Whisper or Cantor of Khemesh.
monastic_tradition.quote: Down there the dark is not empty. It is occupied, and it has all the time there is.
monastic_tradition.debt_resistant_frame: Nothing collects from the deep. The deep only takes. Monks of the Abyssal Maw gain +1 die to resist any binding, geas, or compulsion that would fix them in a place or force them upward. On a success the compulsion does not break — it sinks out of relevance, and whoever laid it feels it go.

basic.name: Crushing Grip
basic.effect: When you successfully grapple or restrain a creature, they suffer –1 die to all actions while grappled and cannot speak or breathe properly (no verbal components).

advanced.name: Pressure Adaptation
advanced.effect: You are immune to underwater combat penalties and gain +1 die to resist drowning or suffocation. Additionally, you may hold your breath for twice as long as normal.

master.name: The Sundering Deep
master.effect: Once per session, you may become an avatar of crushing pressure for one scene. All enemies within Near range act at Desperate Position, and any structure, vessel, or ward you touch begins to fracture as if under immense weight. You may also declare a single enemy 'crushed'—they suffer Harm 2 and are Stunned for one exchange.

monastic_tradition.corruption_note: Monks follow the patron's general Corruption track; the monastic path does not add a second one. Where a tradition needs its own, it must differ from the general track in kind, not degree.

corruption.benefit: Abyssal Resilience: +1 die to resist fear and pressure-based effects.
corruption.cost: Claustrophobic Comfort: Suffer –1 die in open, well-lit spaces or above ground.

corruption.benefit: Crushing Insight: Once/scene, treat a failed Investigation or Arcana roll as a success, but mark 1 SB (Clubs).
corruption.cost: Weight of Knowledge: When you learn a secret someone wanted hidden, test Resolve (DV 3) or gain 1 Fatigue as the abyss presses on you.

corruption.benefit: Silent Hunter: +2 dice to Stealth in dark or confined spaces.
corruption.cost: Voice of the Deep: When speaking normally, your voice sounds distant and hollow, causing –1 die to social rolls requiring warmth or clarity.

corruption.benefit: Pressure Adaptation: Immune to underwater combat penalties; gain +1 die to resist drowning.
corruption.cost: Crushing Presence: Allies within Near range suffer –1 die to morale-based rolls due to your oppressive aura.

corruption.benefit: Abyssal Empathy: Once/session, sense the deepest fear of any creature within Near range (GM tells you one thing they are afraid of).
corruption.cost: Fractured Perception: –1 die to rolls requiring normal vision; the world appears warped and alien. You cannot recover Fatigue from rest while at sea.

corruption.benefit: Maw-Touched: Once/session, extinguish all non-magical light sources in a zone as a free action. Your presence causes light to dim.
corruption.cost: Hunger of the Maw: Mark +2 Obligation when using this power. You are vulnerable to fire (take +1 Harm from fire-based attacks). Each dawn, you must consume something (food, memory, hope) or mark 1 Fatigue.

playstyle_notes.description:
Khemesh suits a table that wants horror to be structural rather than sudden, and enclosing rather than large. The power is slow, heavy, and entirely reliable, and the cost is never paid in the scene where it is incurred — it is paid in the way the other characters gradually sit further away, and in the way rooms in the fiction get smaller around the character without anyone describing them as smaller.

Run him as an absence of negotiation. He does not bargain, explain, or punish. Things simply become true, and by the time anyone objects the room is too cold and too close for the argument to go anywhere.
emphasizes: Weight, not violence — powers that press, hold, and outlast rather than strike
Cold arriving early — the mark shows in other people's behavior before it shows in the character
No terms offered — nothing to appeal to, negotiate with, or be forgiven by
Hunger without appetite — it consumes matter, memory, and hope with the same indifference
The slow room — isolation played out socially, scene by scene, until the character is alone in company

sample_adventure.title: The Sundering of the Deep
sample_adventure.description: A hull is on the shingle, opened from the inside, and the crew is not in it. The only survivor is a cabin boy who will not stop talking about a pressure that sang. The harbormaster wants the whole thing quietly buried before the season's shipping decides otherwise, and the Ordo Artificum has already sent someone, because they believe the ship was carrying a sealed vessel of trench water and they would very much like to know where it is now. So would the Drowned Chorus, who have been on the beach since before the wreck came in.
sample_adventure.quote: The seal is not holding water. Water does not need holding. Break it and find out what it was actually for.
